newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's CN Rail posts Q4 loss after job charge.
newsitem.headline: Canada's CN Rail posts Q4 loss after job charge.

text.p: Canadian National Railway Co., Canada's biggest railroad, on Tuesday posted a fourth-quarter loss after a charge for previously announced job cuts.

Montreal-based CN said it lost C$166 million ($123 million) or C$1.96 ($1.45) a share in the fourth quarter. The loss included a C$365 million ($270 million) charge for actual and planned job cuts totaling 2,250 in 1996 and 1997.
In the year-earlier quarter, CN earned C$23 million ($17 million) or C$0.36 ($0.27) a share after a C$38 million ($28 million) charge to reduce debt.
CN'S fourth-quarter revenues rose to C$1.08 billion ($790 million) from year earlier C$962 million ($712 million).
After 76 years of Canadian government ownership, CN went public in November 1995 in a C$2.3 billion ($1.7 billion) stock issue, Canada's biggest ever.

For full-year 1996, CN's first as a publicly traded company, the railroad earned C$142 million ($105 million) or C$1.67 ($1.24) a share versus a 1995 loss of C$1.1 billion ($814 million) or C$13.49 ($9.98) a share. The 1995 results included an asset writedown of C$1.3 billion ($962 million).
Full-year 1996 revenues rose to C$4.2 billion ($3.1 billion) from C$4.1 billion ($3.0 billion) in 1995.
CN Chief Executive Paul Tellier said in an interview he did not expect CN to post a charge in 1997 for job cuts.
Tellier said he expected CN revenues in Canada and the United States to rise in 1997 at about the rate of gross domestic product growth in both countries.
CN is North America's sixth largest railroad in terms of annual revenues. It has 21,600 employees in Canada and the United States.
